title: August VPN — capacity and health
description: Service capacity and usage count each user gigabit once; the physical figures count every leg and are diagnostic. Bridges are measured by the source node's outbound tag and never added to a pool or to the service figure. A pool rated as a location shows 'aggregate' and its free percentage is an upper bound.

panels.title: 1. Global capacity — service, not infrastructure
panels.description: Service capacity and usage count each user gigabit once: a flow through a bridge is not counted at both of its ends. The physical figures next to them count every leg and exist for planning the plumbing, never as the fleet KPI.

panels.title: Service capacity ↓
panels.description: Summed over the pools users connect to.

panels.title: Service usage ↓
panels.description: Physical usage minus the duplication the bridge counters measure.

panels.title: Attribution
panels.description: Aggregate means at least one pool is rated as a location and a member is missing, so the figure above is an upper bound.

panels.title: Physical capacity ↓ (diagnostic)
panels.description: Every leg of the infrastructure added up, bridges included. A diagnostic for the plumbing, not the capacity of the service: a bridged flow occupies two legs.

panels.title: Physical usage ↓ (diagnostic)
panels.description: The sum of node counters, in which one bridged user flow appears twice. A diagnostic. The service figure to the left is the one the fleet is judged by.

panels.title: Bridged share ↓
panels.description: The part of physical usage that is one user flow counted twice.

panels.title: Nodes disabled
panels.description: Deliberate. Out of capacity, and not an incident.

panels.title: Service vs physical usage ↓
panels.description: Service is the fleet KPI: one user flow counted once. Physical is a diagnostic for the plumbing - it counts the same flow on the ingress node and again on the exit node, and the bridged series is exactly that double count.

panels.title: Service vs physical usage ↑
panels.description: Service is the fleet KPI: one user flow counted once. Physical is a diagnostic for the plumbing - it counts the same flow on the ingress node and again on the exit node, and the bridged series is exactly that double count.

panels.title: 2. Pool status
panels.description: A pool's own resource figure. Where a pool is rated as a location rather than per machine, 'attributed' reads aggregate and the free percentage is an upper bound.

panels.title: 4. Nodes
panels.description: 'shared' means the node's capacity is accounted at its pool because the source data rates the location; 'unmeasured' means nothing is known. They are different states and are shown as such.

panels.title: 5. Bridges — counted by source outbound tag, never added to a pool or to the service figure
6. Connections
panels.description: Established VPN inbound sockets, not users: one user can hold several and a multiplexed client can hold one for many streams. The panel's own online-user count is shown beside them.

panels.title: Host TCP passive opens per second
7. Quotas
panels.description: Nodes with no quota are shown as unlimited and raise no alert.

panels.title: 8. Scaling and recommendation
panels.description: Priority: 1 RED bridge, 2 RED pool, 3 YELLOW bridge, 4 YELLOW pool, 5 overloaded active node. Ties: lowest free %, then lowest absolute free capacity, then highest growth. Sort by rank ascending - the top row is the recommendation.

panels.title: Time to RED at the current trend
panels.description: Empty where the history is too short, the trend is flat or falling, or the series reset. A forecast is not published unless it means something.

panels.title: Growth: short window over long window
panels.description: Gated on having enough samples and a non-zero baseline.

panels.title: 9. Infrastructure and data quality
panels.description: Everything above is only as good as this row is quiet.

panels.title: Network errors and drops per second
TCP retransmit rate
panels.description: Retransmitted segments over sent segments.

panels.title: User port reachability and TCP connect latency
panels.description: Availability from the monitoring host, on the ports users connect to. Packet loss is not measured: nothing here sends ICMP, and inventing a loss figure from a TCP connect would be a number with no source.

panels.title: First observed connected
panels.description: First OBSERVED connection: when this exporter first saw the node connected - not when it first came up. Nothing in the panel records that, and this series starts when the exporter does, so the gap between creation and service cannot be claimed from it.
